tasks.short: Report equipment faults, ensure repairs and make emergency repairs

steps.what: Inspect the actual equipment problem and make emergency repairs when necessary, permitted and possible
inputs: actual equipment fault and operating condition
equipment instructions and permitted repair scope
outputs: actual emergency-repair results and unresolved equipment faults

steps.what: Complete and check the actual equipment-fault report with symptoms, broadcast impact and repairs already attempted
inputs: actual emergency-repair results and unresolved equipment faults
existing equipment asset identity
outputs: complete checked equipment-fault report for the service team

steps.what: Submit the completed equipment-fault report to the internal service team
inputs: complete checked equipment-fault report for the service team

steps.what: Follow the actual repair status with the responsible personnel and verify that the equipment problem is resolved
inputs: submitted equipment-fault report
service team's actual repair updates and equipment repair result
outputs: technician-verified repair resolution or unresolved follow-up need

tasks.design: Configure native asset-linked fault fields and the existing repair-status view in {HELPDESK}. The technician supplies actual symptoms, performs possible emergency repairs and checks the finished report before submitting it, then follows actual service updates and verifies the repair result.
tasks.previous_blocker: Known asset details and repair-status navigation can be repeated during fault handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native service forms and status views can reuse existing asset and repair records.
tasks.still_hard: Emergency repair and proof that the real broadcast fault is resolved require technical judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a ticket marked complete from equipment that actually works correctly.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: asset-linked service forms and repair-status views can reduce known-field entry and navigation while technicians retain actual repair verification.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. Only fixed asset-field entry and status navigation change; repair, follow-up conversation and verification remain.
Asset owners maintain equipment identity; the technician supplies real symptoms/results in s1/s2; the service team supplies actual repair updates, never inferred completion.
Missing or stale status requires manual contact. No new structured fault classification is assumed; existing equivalent configuration removes the gain.
Gross provisional saving 3.4 minus 0.7 hour of form/status-view upkeep gives 2.7 net. Submission is negligible and fully retained.
unknowns: Current service forms and repair-update reliability
research_questions: Which real fault episodes repeat asset entry or status navigation beyond existing native views?

already_counted.description: Write/check actual fault facts and follow/verify repairs

incremental.description: Maintain equipment lookup and repair-status view fields

approvals.approved_version: complete checked equipment-fault report for the service team

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 2.7%; actual repair and resolution checking remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe broadcast monitors and confer with station personnel

steps.what: Observe actual audio/video monitors, levels and off-air return to determine that the programme is airing as intended
inputs: actual audio/video monitors and off-air return
actual programme and level requirements
outputs: technician's actual monitor and airing observations

steps.what: Converse with station personnel about actual audio/video levels, programme airing and any discrepancy
inputs: technician's actual monitor and airing observations
station personnel's actual observations and questions
outputs: actual coordinated understanding of levels and programme airing

tasks.design: Configure the native audio/video and off-air monitor layout in {OTHER}, the broadcast monitoring and station intercom systems. The technician still watches and listens to the real output and talks with station personnel; only repeated monitor-view switching changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate monitor views can require repeated switching to compare airing and levels.
tasks.enabler_now: Native multiview layouts can group existing monitored sources.
tasks.still_hard: A present signal does not prove the intended programme and acceptable sound are actually airing.
tasks.human_edge: Connect monitor evidence with the station team's actual operational context.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native broadcast multiview layouts can reduce view switching while actual output checking and station conversation remain human.

assumptions: Shares are provisional human monitoring effort, not programme duration.
OTHER means broadcast monitors and station intercom. Existing receivers/monitoring systems provide actual return signals; no new telemetry or automatic airing inference is assumed.
Only view switching changes. Missing return signals require normal technical investigation; existing equivalent layouts remove the gain.
Gross provisional saving 3.25 minus 0.5 hour of layout upkeep gives 2.75 net. No written report, send or machine adjustment is proposed by this observation/conversation task.
unknowns: Current monitor layout and true switching effort
research_questions: Can native layout configuration remove repeated switching while keeping all actual output checks?

already_counted.description: Watch/listen to actual monitored output and assess airing

incremental.description: Check monitored-source assignments and layout settings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 2.75%; actual signal observation and station conversation stay fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor broadcast signal quality and adjust equipment

steps.what: Monitor actual incoming/outgoing signal strength, clarity and reliability using the installed monitors and meters
inputs: actual incoming/outgoing signals and installed meters
actual broadcast quality requirements

steps.what: Diagnose the actual quality issue and select the exact permitted equipment adjustment
inputs: technician's actual signal-quality observations
equipment capabilities and permitted operating limits

steps.what: Apply the selected equipment adjustment and check its actual effect on broadcast quality
inputs: technician-selected broadcast-equipment adjustment
actual broadcast equipment and signal
outputs: actual adjusted equipment and checked signal response

tasks.design: Retain actual signal-quality assessment and equipment adjustment with the technician using {OTHER}, the installed broadcast monitor/control equipment. No supported new telemetry, approved control feature or monitor-navigation change is established for this task, so no labour saving is claimed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual signal defects require diagnosis and equipment-specific intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional verified change to the installed monitoring/control work is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults and perceptual quality cannot be established by one meter value.
tasks.human_edge: Diagnose the real cause and choose a permitted adjustment without degrading another signal path.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: broadcast quality diagnosis and equipment adjustment require evidence about the actual installed system before software savings can be claimed.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. Existing monitors/meters produce the actual observed readings; no new structured telemetry is assumed.
Observation, adjustment selection and control action are separate and fully retained. No report or log is specified here; transmitter logging is separately represented in task 18653.
Each actual adjustment follows the technician's selected setting. A changed setting requires another decision.
No system change is proposed, so gross/net saving are zero and there is no incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Installed monitoring/control capabilities and actual faults
research_questions: Does the actual equipment offer an approved native feature that removes a specific human monitoring/control action?

incremental.description: No new monitoring or control system proposed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No supported change to actual signal observation, diagnosis or control work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor and log actual transmitter readings

steps.what: Monitor and inspect actual transmitter readings and identify the transmitter and observation time
inputs: actual transmitter meters/readings
actual transmitter identity and observation time
outputs: technician-observed transmitter readings with identity and time

steps.what: Enter the actual readings into the transmitter log and check the complete log entry, units, identity and time
inputs: technician-observed transmitter readings with identity and time
actual available native meter telemetry with units and timestamps

steps.what: Save the completed checked transmitter-log entry in the existing log application
inputs: complete checked transmitter-log entry

tasks.design: Configure native draft-log population from actual available readings in {OTHER}, the transmitter monitoring/log application. The technician still monitors the transmitter, checks every populated value and timestamp against the real observation, then saves the completed log entry; no automatic commit is hidden in population.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual meter readings may be manually transcribed despite existing native telemetry.
tasks.enabler_now: A native draft-log function can reuse actual telemetry values and source metadata.
tasks.still_hard: A reading can be stale, mismapped or in the wrong units even when it fills a valid field.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise whether the actual reading and transmitter state make sense.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native transmitter telemetry can populate draft log fields where supported, with technician verification of values, identity, units and freshness.

assumptions: Shares are a provisional manual-log-entry scenario, not measured baseline evidence. Monitoring remains fully retained.

OTHER means transmitter monitoring/log software. Existing instrument telemetry must supply transmitter ID, parameter, value, unit and timestamp; the technician checks these against the actual observation in s1/s2.
Missing, stale or unmatched telemetry returns the entry to manual transcription. No new sensor feed, reason code or inferred normal/fault label is assumed.
Native configuration is required before custom integration; unsupported draft population or existing automatic logs remove the corresponding gain.
Gross provisional saving 20.65 minus 2 hours of telemetry-field/freshness configuration upkeep gives 18.65 net. Save is negligible and fully retained.
unknowns: Actual native draft-log capability, telemetry coverage and current manual entry
research_questions: Can the existing native log draft reproduce actual readings with correct units and timestamps while reducing total entry/checking work?

already_counted.description: Supply/check actual values and complete the log entry

incremental.description: Maintain telemetry-field mappings and test freshness/unit checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 18.65%; requires existing supported telemetry and real manual transcription remaining today.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

skills_to_grow: Verify transmitter log provenance and freshness
